\section{Spectral and image representations}\label{sec:formulas}

\begin{proposition}[Character expansion]\label{prop:character}
For $t>0$ the central heat kernel with respect to Haar probability is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:character}
 p_t(\theta)=\sum_{n=0}^{\infty}(n+1)e^{-n(n+2)t/2}
 \frac{\sin((n+1)\theta)}{\sin\theta},
\end{equation}
with the endpoint values understood by continuity.  The series and all its
spatial derivatives converge normally for $t$ bounded below by a positive
number, and $\int p_t\dd H=1$.
\end{proposition}

\begin{proof}
Peter--Weyl expansion of the delta mass supplies the coefficient $n+1$;
the declared generator supplies the exponential eigenvalue.  Character
orthogonality leaves only the trivial representation after Haar integration.
\end{proof}

\begin{proposition}[Poisson-image formula]\label{prop:image}
For $0<\theta<\pi$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:image}
 p_t(\theta)=C_t\frac{1}{\sin\theta}
 \sum_{k\in\mathbb Z}(\theta+2\pi k)
 e^{-(\theta+2\pi k)^2/(2t)},
 \qquad C_t=\frac{e^{t/2}\sqrt{2\pi}}{2t^{3/2}}.
\end{equation}
Both endpoints have removable limits after the appropriate images are paired.
Equations~\eqref{eq:character} and \eqref{eq:image} agree exactly for every
$t>0$.
\end{proposition}

The proof by differentiated Poisson summation is given in
Appendix~\ref{app:poisson}.  Formula~\eqref{eq:character} is stable for
moderate and large time.  Formula~\eqref{eq:image} is stable at small time
away from the antipode.  Near the antipode one must first pair the two shortest
images.

For $a_k=2\pi k$, factor the zero image in \eqref{eq:image}:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:factorization}
 p_t(\theta)=C_t e^{-\theta^2/(2t)}\frac{\theta}{\sin\theta}
 (1+q_t(\theta)),
\end{equation}
where the paired correction is
\begin{equation}\label{eq:q}
q_t(\theta)=2\sum_{k\ge1}e^{-a_k^2/(2t)}
\left[\cosh\frac{a_k\theta}{t}
-\frac{a_k}{\theta}\sinh\frac{a_k\theta}{t}\right].
\end{equation}
At $\theta=0$ the quotient is interpreted by its even Taylor series.
